newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end lower, snapping record streak.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end lower, snapping record streak.

text.p: Swiss shares ended 1.4 percent lower, pushing the Swiss Market Index (SMI) below the 5,700 point level on Monday and ending a three-day record run.
A lack of follow-through buying, profit taking and derivatives-linked transactions were behind the retreat that put a limp end to the powerful rally in the first half of the year, dealers said.
The market was seen cautious ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting on July 1 and 2 that will play a big role determining the direction of U.S. interest rates.
"Further development will depend on Wall Street," one dealer said.
The blue-chip SMI was down 79.7 points, or 1.4 percent, at 5,620.6. The broad Swiss Performance Index closed down 45.14 points, or 1.26 percent, to 3,548.37.
Actively traded Novartis registered shares fell 29 francs to 2,334. Roche gave up 225 francs to 13,205.
Among banks, Credit Suisse slumped 8.50 francs, or 4.34 percent, to 187.50. SBC gave up five francs to 390.50.
Dealers said the two banks came under pressure after recent rumours that they could merge parts of their activities were not substantiated.
Zurich Group lost 19 francs to 581. UBS left its rating at "hold" for the insurer's shares in light of its planned acqquisition of U.S. asset manager Scudder, Stevens & Clark.

Alusuisse registered shares were among the few winners in the blue-chip segment. Dealers said there were rumours the company could announce a spin-off of a division or a unified share structure at a briefing on July 4.

Sulzer was down 22 francs to 1,250. Sulzer Medica, its medical technology subsidiary which is going public in July, said it expected its rate of return on sales to decline again this year before rising in 1998.
Among other industrials, ABB ended down 10 francs at 2,210. Clariant and Ciba were up.
